Evidence Profile — Medium confidence

Weakest-link rule: overall confidence follows the lowest-scoring applicable dimension (Moderate, from "Spatial robustness").

Observation completenessGood

12 Sentinel-2 / 5 Landsat cloud-free scenes - meets the minimum (3/3) but with little margin.

Spatial robustnessModerate

Only 9 of 21 flagged pair(s) remained significant after spatial correction - most were likely clustering artefacts.

Temporal representativenessGood

SUHI stayed within 0.7°C across 3 summers (this run + 2 prior year(s)) - consistent across 3 years — approaching, but still short of, the 30-year WMO climate-normal standard (Landsat 8/9's 2013 launch is the practical ceiling on how far back this check can go).

Data freshnessExcellent

Analysis window ends 0 month(s) ago.

Hazard

R1 Urban Heat Island Urban Heat Island (moderate) Triggered 0.79
SUHI 7.581 °C threshold 4
threshold is self-calibrated for this city (max of the 2°C literature baseline and 1.5× this run's own non-urban temperature std dev (σ=3.07°C)), not a flat constant applied to every climate.
LST_urban 41.839 °C
LST_nonUrban 34.257 °C
Monitor and consider gradual cooling interventions - the heat island is present but not yet at a critical level.
R10 Dangerous Heat Index Heat index - extreme caution Triggered 0.57
HEAT_INDEX_urban 32.703 °C threshold 27
NOAA/NWS Heat Index (Rothfusz regression), from ERA5-Land 2m air temperature + dewpoint - a public, documented formula and public comfort/danger thresholds, not a per-city calibration. Resolution caveat: ERA5-Land's native grid is ~11km, far coarser than the satellite-derived indicators elsewhere in this report - treat this as a city-wide climatological reading, not a fine-grained map the way LST/NDVI are.
Heat index sits in NOAA's "extreme caution" band - not yet dangerous, but worth factoring into outdoor-activity guidance during the hottest part of the day. Cross-check against R8 (cooling capacity) to see which areas would benefit most from added shade or water features.
R11 Flood Risk No significant flood risk detected Below threshold 0.00
COASTAL_FLOOD_RISK_INDEX 0 index (0-1) threshold 0.15
Deltares coastal flood hazard (100-year return period, present-day sea level, GTSMv3.0 tide/storm surge model, externally validated) x population exposure - coastal flooding only, doesn't cover river flooding (see FLOOD_RISK_INDEX for that).
PLUVIAL_RUNOFF_RISK 0.038 index (0-1) threshold 0.5
impervious surface fraction x terrain flatness - a proxy for urban flash-flood/stormwater risk in areas with no mapped river hazard, not itself an external hazard product like the river/coastal evidence above.

R3 Poor Green Space Accessibility Limited green space access Triggered 0.52
pct_pop_near_green_300m 48.425 % threshold 50
standard EU threshold (Eurostat/EEA): access = under 300m from green space
Access below the EU standard - identify densely populated areas with no green space within 300m.
R8 Low Cooling Capacity Critical cooling capacity deficit Triggered 0.50
CCI_urban 0.014 index (0-1) threshold 0.076
CCI = 0.3*NDVI_norm + 0.3*tree canopy + 0.2*water - 0.2*impervious (Dynamic World "built"), clamped 0-1 - the weights are a starting judgement call, not fitted. Update: cross-city regression testing initially found the impervious-fraction term's sign inconsistent with the expected physical relationship on both targets tested (SUHI, LST_urban). A land-cover compositing defect (D-05, CHANGELOG 0.1.2) was found and fixed, and on a small 3-city sample the SUHI sign corrected itself and a fitted model briefly appeared to beat the naive heuristic (R² 0.301->0.417) - this did NOT hold up on a larger, 7-city sample (R² fell to -0.407, worse than the mean) and is retracted; SUHI's status here is OPEN, not resolved. The coefficient's corrected sign (positive) does still hold on the larger sample. On LST_urban, adding each city's own background (non-urban) temperature as a covariate corrected the sign and, on the same larger 7-city sample, reached R²=0.884 - a genuinely strong result, not just a partial one. Elevation was tested directly as a candidate confound and ruled out on both targets. Stopping rule in force: no further covariates are tested on the current sample - only reconfirmation on an even larger, more climatically diverse set changes this status.
Very little vegetation, canopy or water relative to impervious surface - this area has almost no passive cooling infrastructure. Cross-check against R1/R2 for whether it also runs hot in practice.
R4 Green Space Fragmentation Green space reasonably consolidated Below threshold 0.00
green_largest_patch_index_pct 81.458 % threshold 20
green_patch_count 267 count
R6 Population-Weighted Green Deficit Vegetation adequate relative to population Below threshold 0.00
GDI_urban 0.175 index (0-1) threshold 0.18
GDI = (1 - normalised NDVI) x normalised population - only high where both are true together: little vegetation AND a lot of people

Both p-values are Bonferroni-corrected for the number of rule pairs tested this run. "Survives" means the co-occurrence held up after a spatial-permutation correction (not just a naive Fisher's exact test) - neighbouring zones are spatially autocorrelated by construction, so a naive test alone would overstate significance. Moran's I (0 = scattered/random, approaching 1 = strongly clustered) is shown for each rule's own mask independently - it's a diagnostic explaining WHY a naive test can overstate significance for a highly self-clustered rule, not itself a significance test; "n/a" means it couldn't be computed for that mask (too few populated cells, or a degenerate mask).

#1 — Zone 34,40

R1 — Urban Heat Island (severe) (confidence 0.95)
Prioritise cooling interventions (shading, reflective surfaces, vegetation) in the hottest urban zones - SUHI is above this city's calibrated severe threshold (5°C).
R2 — Critical heat exposure (confidence 0.88)
Areas that are dense AND hot at the same time - a health risk during heatwaves. Top priority for cooling + thermal shelter.
R3 — Critical green space deficit (confidence 0.88)
Under 25% of the population has green access within 300m - high priority for pocket parks in the uncovered areas.
R9 — Severely sprawling/fragmented urban shape (confidence 0.8)
The built-up area is elongated, irregular or scattered across many disconnected patches rather than one consolidated footprint - this is a different signal from R5 (which only measures how much area was added). Sprawling/fragmented shape usually means longer infrastructure and service lines per resident; worth checking whether new growth (R5, if triggered) is making this better or worse.
R6 — Critical green deficit (confidence 0.67)
Vegetation is close to absent in a densely populated area - a resident here can be technically "within 300m" of a park (see R3) and still live surrounded by almost no greenery day to day. Prioritise street trees and small green infrastructure directly in the built fabric, not just a park at the neighbourhood edge.
R10 — Heat index - extreme caution (confidence 0.57)
Heat index sits in NOAA's "extreme caution" band - not yet dangerous, but worth factoring into outdoor-activity guidance during the hottest part of the day. Cross-check against R8 (cooling capacity) to see which areas would benefit most from added shade or water features.
R7 — Critical tree canopy deficit (confidence 0.55)
Tree canopy is close to absent over the urban area - prioritise street trees and canopy planting, not just park-level green space (see R3/R6 for where people actually are relative to any green at all).
R8 — Critical cooling capacity deficit (confidence 0.52)
Very little vegetation, canopy or water relative to impervious surface - this area has almost no passive cooling infrastructure. Cross-check against R1/R2 for whether it also runs hot in practice.
R5 — Detectable recent urban growth (confidence 0.45)
Detectable urban growth over the last decade near this run's epoch - worth tracking in future runs.
